headline: A $6.4B Binance hack and FBI attribution to North Korea rattle crypto as Bitcoin tests $76K
summary: The week's defining story is a record $6.4 billion exploit on Binance, now attributed by the FBI to North Korea's TraderTraitor hacking group — triggering $5.3 billion in net outflows from the exchange and pushing the Fear & Greed index to 26. Bitcoin briefly dipped to $76,300 before recovering to $77,324, on track for a fifth consecutive weekly loss. Privacy coins split: Monero gained 3.2% as traders sought assets with stronger on-chain anonymity, while Zcash fell nearly 6% as lower-liquidity coins bore the brunt of the fear-driven selloff.

winners.name: Monero
winners.catalyst: Monero gained as the Binance hack and broader exchange security concerns drove renewed interest in privacy-preserving assets. The FBI's attribution of the $6.4B Binance hack to North Korea's TraderTraitor group may have amplified demand for coins with stronger on-chain anonymity.

losers.name: Zcash
losers.catalyst: Zcash fell sharply despite sharing privacy-coin characteristics with top mover XMR, suggesting rotation within the privacy-coin sector rather than a broad thematic bid. Continued market-wide fear — Fear & Greed at 26 and BTC facing a fifth consecutive weekly loss — weighed disproportionately on lower-liquidity assets.

whyItMoved:
The week's dominant force is a $6.4 billion exploit on Binance — the largest exchange hack on record — which the FBI has formally attributed to North Korea's TraderTraitor hacking group. Binance reported cumulative net outflows of $5.3 billion as users pulled funds in response, though the exchange's CEO stated recovery is underway and published a fresh proof-of-reserves snapshot to reassure remaining depositors. North Korea's government, through Kim Jong-Un's sister, publicly denied involvement, adding a geopolitical dimension to an already unsettled market.

Bitcoin touched $76,300 during the session before recovering to $77,324, a -0.75% move on the day that understates the week's cumulative pressure. Persistent ETF outflows and uncertainty around U.S. midterm elections have kept sentiment deeply negative — the Fear & Greed index sits at 26, firmly in fear territory, and Bitcoin is on pace for a fifth straight weekly loss.

The hack's clearest market signal was a split within privacy coins. Monero rose 3.2% as traders rotated toward assets with stronger built-in transaction anonymity — the logic being that Monero's privacy architecture is more robust than Zcash's optional shielding. Zcash fell 5.8%, suggesting this was a targeted rotation rather than a broad privacy-coin bid. Lower-liquidity assets across the board absorbed more of the fear-driven selling pressure. XRP and TRON bucked the trend with modest gains of 2.4% and 1.6% respectively, though no specific catalyst was identified for either move beyond relative resilience in a down session.
worthKnowing: Liquid Network's bitcoin IOUs are fully collateralized again after a $320 million exploit was remediated — a rare clean resolution in a week dominated by exchange security failures.
Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin suffered a hack of approximately $46 million and pledged to cover all affected user losses in full.
Binance completed a fresh proof-of-reserves snapshot following the $5.3 billion in net outflows, with the CEO stating the exchange's recovery is in progress.
North Korea's government publicly denied FBI claims attributing the Binance hack to the TraderTraitor group, adding geopolitical uncertainty to the ongoing fallout.
